descriptor:
Italian specialty pharmaceutical group · Specialty & Primary Care + Rare Diseases · FY ends 31 December · reported in EUR

⚠LIVE TAKE-PRIVATE TENDER OFFER — this is a merger-arbitrage situation, not a standalone growth equity. CVC Fund IX + Groupe Bruxelles Lambert, via Respighi BidCo, are offering €51.29/share ex-dividend (€52.00 cum-dividend, ~€10.7bn total) for all shares. Rossini S.àr.l. (CVC's vehicle, 46.82%) has irrevocably committed to tender; CONSOB approved the offer document 8-Jul-2026. Acceptance period: 31-Aug-2026 to 15-Oct-2026. A full squeeze-out needs ≥66.67%. Six of ten directors called the offer fair; four independent directors dissented as inadequate. Current price €52.65 is ABOVE the €51.29 offer — a bet on a bump, not a discount for deal risk. Deal-state weighted IV is €50.47 (−4.1% vs price) across three scenarios: completes at €51.29 (78% weight), bumped to €55.50 (12%), breaks to ~€43.65 (10%). Risk/reward is 4.6:1 against (lose €9.54 on a break to make €2.05 on a bump); a buyer needs ~67% probability of a bump just to break even against a realistic 10% break risk. Conclusion: AVOID at €52.65 — holders should tender or sell above the offer; the DCF section below is the standalone/no-deal anchor, not a live trading signal.

sections.title: Growth & Profitability
sections.subtitle: FY2015-18 figures are pre-audit highlights (income statement only); balance sheet, cash flow and EPS begin FY2019 — both eras normalized to €m here

sections.title: Owner Cash Flow & Capital Allocation
sections.subtitle: the standalone crux: how much of reported cash flow is genuinely distributable once bolt-on M&A/licence spend needed to keep growing is charged

charts.title: Reported FCF vs Owner FCF
charts.annotation: Owner FCF point is from the DCF JSON (inputs.last_fcf), not the CSV: FY2025 reported FCF was €511.8m but only €359m is sustainable once product-rights replenishment capex (~6.5% of revenue, the observed intangible amortisation rate) is charged alongside 1.5% maintenance PP&E. Over FY2019-25 Recordati converted €3,327.8m of operating cash flow into just €1,180.3m of owner FCF.

charts.title: CapEx (Lumpy, M&A-Driven)
charts.annotation: CapEx is NOT a maintenance run-rate: FY2024's €851.2m includes the Enjaymo product-rights acquisition vs FY2025's €85.1m quiet year. Reading either year in isolation misprices the business.

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Total consolidated sales across Recordati's Specialty & Primary Care and Rare Diseases segments, ~150 countries.

For Recordati: FY2015-18 figures come from pre-audit highlights tables and cover the income statement only; FY2019 onward come from audited statements. Both eras are normalized to €m here so the FY2018→FY2019 transition (€1,352.2m → €1,481.8m) reads as the smooth continuation it is, not a reporting-scale artefact.

What to watch:

  • Mature Specialty & Primary Care brands erode organically (Cardicor licence loss, lercanidipine generic erosion, Seloken -12.8% in H1-2026) and must be replaced by bolt-on M&A
  • Rare Diseases growth is concentrated in Isturisa, whose US peak-sales guidance was recently doubled on an expanded Cushing's label
  • FY2026 guidance midpoint is €2.73-2.80bn revenue

margins.title: Gross, Operating & EBITDA Margin
margins.content:
Gross margin (revenue less cost of goods), operating margin (after opex) and EBITDA margin (before interest, tax, D&A) show how much of each sales euro survives to the operating line.

For Recordati: gross margin has held remarkably stable near 68-72% across a decade of acquisitions. FY2025 EBITDA margin was 37.8% (company-reported, before significant items) — the EBITDA margin line here is derived as reported EBITDA / revenue for years the company-reported figure isn't separately disclosed, so it will differ slightly from management's own 37.0-37.8% in FY2024-25.

What to watch: margin resilience through integration of newly-acquired rare-disease assets, which typically carry high gross margins but front-loaded launch/commercial costs.

netIncome.title: Net Income & Net Margin
netIncome.content:
Bottom-line statutory profit after interest, tax, D&A and acquisition-related amortisation, and net margin as a % of revenue.

For Recordati: net margin has compressed from ~23-25% pre-2022 to ~15-19% since, as debt-funded acquisitions (EUSA Pharma, Enjaymo rights, Vazkepa licence) added interest expense and intangible amortisation ahead of the revenue they bought.

What to watch: whether rare-disease revenue growth outruns the amortisation drag as newly-acquired assets mature.

eps.title: Earnings Per Share
eps.content:
Diluted EPS in euros (not cents).

For Recordati: FY2025 EPS was €2.159, up from €2.019 in FY2024. The share count is flat-to-shrinking (204.8m at H1-2026 vs 206.3m FY2024) — Recordati is a net repurchaser (€157.1m of FY2025 treasury purchases against €16.5m of SBC), so EPS growth is not diluted away.

What to watch: under the live tender offer, EPS trajectory is irrelevant to a holder who tenders into the fixed €51.29 cash offer.

ownerFcf.title: Reported FCF vs Owner FCF
ownerFcf.content:
Reported FCF = operating cash flow less capex, as disclosed. Owner FCF further deducts a product-rights replenishment charge the DCF model applies at 6.5% of revenue (the observed intangible amortisation rate) plus 1.5% maintenance PP&E, instead of whatever capex Recordati happened to spend that year.

For Recordati: the two numbers diverge enormously because growth here is bought, not organic. FY2025 reported FCF was €511.8m (a quiet M&A year, capex only 3.3% of revenue) but sustainable owner FCF is €359m. FY2024 reported FCF was negative €281.2m (the €814.5m Enjaymo intangible purchase alone). Over FY2019-25 Recordati converted €3,327.8m of operating cash flow into only €1,180.3m of owner FCF — capex absorbed 15.5% of revenue in aggregate. Treating any single year's reported capex as a run-rate misprices the business in either direction.

What to watch: whether replenishment spend can fall as the Rare Diseases book matures and organic growth from Isturisa's expanded label reduces the need for further bolt-ons.

capex.title: Capital Expenditure
capex.content:
Combined PP&E and intangible (product-rights, licence) capital spend, as reported.

For Recordati: maintenance PP&E is remarkably stable at 1.3-1.6% of revenue, but total capex swings from 1.7% to 34.8% of revenue year to year because it is dominated by lumpy M&A/in-licensing (FY2024's €851.2m includes the Enjaymo rights purchase; FY2025's €85.1m was a quiet year with almost none). Reading either extreme as a run-rate is the single most consequential error an analyst can make on this business — see the Owner FCF chart.

What to watch: the next bolt-on acquisition, not the current-year capex print.

netDebt.title: Total Debt & Cash
netDebt.content:
Interest-bearing debt and cash balances. Net debt = total debt less cash.

For Recordati: FY2025 net debt was €2,038.7m (total debt €2,467.5m less cash €428.8m), close to the company's own Net Financial Position of €2,037.3m. Debt stepped up sharply from FY2021 (€992m) to FY2022 (€1,717m) funding the EUSA Pharma acquisition, and again through the Enjaymo/Vazkepa deals.

What to watch: under the tender offer, existing leverage is the acquirer's problem post-completion, not a standalone risk for a holder tendering at €51.29.

sbc.title: Stock-Based Compensation
sbc.content:
Non-cash expense for equity-settled incentive plans, already embedded inside reported EBITDA as an operating cost (not added back separately in the DCF).

For Recordati: SBC is tiny relative to revenue — €16.5m in FY2025, just 0.63% of revenue, a fraction of what a typical US tech issuer reports. H1-2026's €23.6m is a one-off: the takeover accelerated performance-share vesting, not a new run-rate.

What to watch: nothing material — SBC does not move the valuation here.
